conflict_topics: privacy for pumping (private use of room)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants provide concrete reasons (client calls, private calls, file access) and practical proposals (time shifts, moving boxes).
There is some needless repetition of short acknowledgements (many "Okay, thanks." / "Great.").
Speakers stay consistent about physical constraints and roles (who uses the room and why).
evaluation.final_reason: Parties agreed concrete schedule adjustments and a material accommodation: Agent D moved the 1pm slot to 12:30 and the afternoon request to 3:30 (Agent D: "I can come a bit earlier, like 12:30." and earlier A accepted 3:30), and Agent B agreed to relocate the daily-use boxes out of the room (Agent B: "They can go next to my desk."), with Agent D explicitly accepting the repeated proposal (Agent D: "Yes, that's a great idea. That would work perfectly. Thanks, Agent B."). These explicit statements show who adjusted what and what was asked in return.
position_change_notes: Agent D adjusted requested times when told of clashes: proposed 3:30 for the afternoon and 12:30 for the midday slot (D: "Is 3.30 okay?"; "I can come a bit earlier, like 12:30.").

Agent B moved from objection to active accommodation: initially objected to locking ("If the room is locked I can't get my work done."), then proposed and agreed to moving boxes ("They can go next to my desk.").
Agent C conceded their 1pm slot when D proposed 12:30 (C: "Yes, 12:30 works for me.").
Agent A agreed to the adjusted afternoon time (A: "Yes, 3.30 works.").

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: "The 1 p.m. should be fine. But I often have client calls in that room from 4 p.m. onwards. Can you do the afternoon one any earlier?"; Agent D: "Yes, I can. Is 3.30 okay?" — Scheduling incompatibility about the afternoon slot is raised and a counter-proposal is made but not yet confirmed.

Agent B: "I'm in and out of that room all day for the files. If the room is locked I can't get my work done." — A substantive access/operational conflict appears (privacy/locking vs B's file access) and is unresolved at the end of the round.

Agent C: "Agent D, the 1 p.m. slot is a problem. I use that room for a private call every day around that time."; Agent D: "I can come a bit earlier, like 12:30."; Agent D to B: "it's only for fifteen minutes. I do need the privacy." — The 1 p.m. scheduling conflict is addressed (D offers 12:30), but B's access concern remains unresolved.

Agent B: "If I'm blocked for fifteen minutes, my work stops. Can we move the boxes I use daily out of that room?"; Agent C: "Yes, 12:30 works for me." — B proposes a concrete mitigation (moving boxes); scheduling conflict with C appears resolved, but the access issue is pending implementation.

Agent D: "Okay, 12:30 is fine. ... Moving the boxes you need daily sounds like a good idea. Where can they go?"; Agent B: "They can go next to my desk. That should keep them out of the main walkway." — Parties agree on new times (12:30 and 3:30) and a concrete relocation for the boxes, settling the key incompatibilities.
Agent B repeats: "They can go next to my desk."; Agent D: "Okay, that works." — Confirmation/repetition after the agreement; no new substantive conflict.
Agent B: "Okay, thanks." (repeated) — No substantive disagreement or new issues raised.

Agent B: "I get that, but I can't predict when I'll need a file. What if we move the boxes I use every day out of that room? Then you can have it whenever. Half of those are old files anyway." — B restates/unpacks unpredictability and again proposes moving boxes; this reopens the operational issue until accepted.
Agent D: "Yes, that's a great idea. That would work perfectly. Thanks, Agent B."; Agent B: "Great." — The reiterated proposal is explicitly accepted, removing the remaining incompatibility.
Agent B: "Great." (repeated) — No substantive disagreement; closure language only.

substantive_insights: Two separate conflicts existed: scheduling conflicts among users and an operational access conflict about files and locking; both required different solutions.
Resolution combined schedule changes (D moved to 12:30 and 3:30) and a physical accommodation (B agreed to relocate boxes), distributing adjustment across parties.
B's recurring concern about unpredictability was handled by relocating boxes to allow short, locked uses without stopping B's workflow.
